scope: Independent IDE correctness fixes found while investigating native Win98 file-cache corruption; not a claimed root-cause fix.
changes: LBA28 advancement selects bits24..27 for the head, rather than the low address nibble, and keeps Device register readback synchronized for LBA28 and CHS.
LBA48 advancement preserves all six task-file bytes and carries above2^32 sectors; sector-count subtraction wraps at the command-defined8/16-bit width.
READ MULTIPLE initial progress uses the actual DRQ block size rather than CHS sectors-per-track.
WRITE MULTIPLE accepts both command forms and advances each subsequent DRQ by a whole configured block, bounded by the final partial block.

regression.before: Four isolated old-source groups fail: selected-head reuse,task-file carries,initial multiple-read block progress,multiple-write IRQ boundaries.
regression.selectedHeadExample: Without a second Device write,the old implementation reads byte8628117504 instead of38182912 for the next request.
regression.multipleWriteExample: Four-sector mode,ten sectors: old IRQ boundaries4,5,6,7,8,9,10; corrected4,8,10.
regression.after: Source and release pass: real payload addresses,selected-head reuse,LBA28/48 carries,CHS sector/head/cylinder wrap,zero-count256-sector reads,multiple read/write boundaries,counts,and every written word.
regression.release: Closure0errors/0warnings; release transfer-progress,large-disk and33-case AHCI all pass.

limits: Currently running native benchmarks loaded the earlier IDE module and do not acquire this change through rebuilding.
The new transfer regression establishes these device bugs; fresh native testing is still required before connecting them to Win98 resource corruption.
No DAT,driver,benchmark bytes or original disk image is changed.
